subject: Architecture
title: The Burj Khalifa: Reaching 2,717 Feet
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Burj Khalifa: Reaching 2,717 Feet.

hook.text: The Burj Khalifa is so tall that the temperature at the top is 10°F cooler than at the base.

buildup.text: Its Y-shaped floor plan resists wind forces that would topple a rectangular building of equal height.

discovery.text: The tower sways up to 6 feet at the top in strong winds. Occupants on the highest floors can feel it.

twist.text: Dubai ran out of money during construction. Abu Dhabi bailed it out — hence the name Khalifa.

climax.text: It took 22 million work hours and 12,000 workers per day at peak construction.

punchline.text: It needed a bailout. Now it prints money from tourists.

quiz.question: Why does the Burj Khalifa have a Y-shaped floor plan?
options: To maximize the number of corner offices
To resist wind forces at extreme height
To create a distinctive silhouette from the ground

details.summary: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai stands 828 meters tall with 163 floors, making it the world's tallest structure by a wide margin since its 2010 opening. Its Y-shaped floor plan and buttressed core design reduce wind forces, while the tapered profile ensures the tower sheds vortices at different heights.
details.whyItMatters: The Burj Khalifa pushed every engineering discipline to new limits — structural, mechanical, elevator, and construction technology all required innovation. It proved that engineering can solve problems at scales previously considered impossible.
takeaways: Stands 828 meters tall with 163 floors since 2010
Y-shaped floor plan reduces wind forces on the tower
Tapered profile prevents dangerous wind vortex synchronization

faq.question: How does the Burj Khalifa handle wind?
faq.answer: The Y-shaped plan confuses wind into flowing around different shapes at different angles. The tower steps back 26 times as it rises, preventing vortex shedding from synchronizing. Without these features, the building would sway dangerously and generate a low-frequency hum.

faq.question: How long do the elevators take to reach the top?
faq.answer: The fastest elevators travel at 10 meters per second, reaching the observation deck on the 124th floor in about one minute. No single elevator runs the full height — sky lobbies at several floors require transfers, similar to changing trains in a subway system.
